newsitem.title: FRANCE: French paper estimates 97 deficit at 270 bln Ffr.
newsitem.headline: French paper estimates 97 deficit at 270 bln Ffr.

text.p: France's central government budget deficit next year is likely to be between 265 and 275 billion francs, overshooting an unofficial target fixed earlier this year, financial daily Les Echos said on Wednesday.
The government said earlier this year it planned to limit the central government budget deficit to 248 billion francs.
Les Echos gave no source for its estimate and government officials were not immediately available for comment.
But Finance Minister Jean Arthuis told reporters last week that the 1997 budget due to be presented on September 18 would contain a deficit total before tax cuts and a deficit total after tax cuts.

That would suggest that lost revenue from 25 billion francs in income tax cuts promised for next year would have to be added to the original deficit target -- bringing the deficit to around 275 billion francs.

But some of that lost revenue will be recouped through higher duties on alcohol and tobacco, and to a lesser extent, on petrol, which economists estimate could raise anything between five and 10 billion francs -- bringing the deficit back down towards 265 billion francs.

Government officials have repeatedly refused to comment on the size of the central government budget deficit next year but have said that spending will be frozen at this year's targetted 1,552 billion francs.
Since spending on some areas will rise automatically -- to cover inflation, debt service charges and pre-agreed civil service promotions -- deep spending cuts are expected elsewhere.

An overshooting in the central government budget deficit would not necessarily prevent France from reducing the total public deficit to three percent of gross domestic product next year as planned to meet Maastricht treaty standards.

The government is also raising some seven billion francs in additional taxes to fund the separately run welfare system, and has access to a range of other sources of revenue on accounts held outside the central government budget.
